commands.title: Ask an agent to add a trigger
commands.description: Start an agent session that asks you what the trigger should wait for and do, then adds it, and show it in Agents.

commands.title: Add trigger
commands.description: Call an agent-visible command whenever a bus event of this workspace arrives, e.g. have a reviewer session look at another session's work when its turn ends: on agents.turn, match {"session":"<coder id>","status":"done"}, command agents.prompt, args {"session":"<reviewer id>","text":"Review what {{payload.session}} just did"}. Clubmate already prompts you when your own child sessions end their turns, so don't add triggers for that. To follow the sessions a cron job or trigger starts with agents.new, whatever their ids: on agents.turn, match {"cronJob":"cj_…","finished":true} (or "trigger":"tr_…"); finished is true only when the session's turn ended done with no child session still running or waiting. Only events naming this workspace (in workspace, workspaceId or session.workspaceId) fire it. String values in args may hold {{topic}}, {{seq}}, {{payload}} and {{payload.<field.path>}}, filled from the event. The target command and its args are checked now. A trigger never runs twice at once unless parallel is true; more runs within 1m than limit (default 10) or 3 errors in a row pause it. triggers.* and cron.* commands cannot be targets. Returns the trigger: {id, name, workspace, on, match?, command, args, enabled, limit?, parallel?, owner?, createdBy?, failures?, lastError?}. Non-destructive.

name.description: Short human name of the trigger.

on.description: Bus topic to listen to, e.g. agents.turn, or a prefix pattern, e.g. event.*; * alone is not allowed. triggers.emit {name} publishes event.<name>.

match.description: Payload filter as JSON text (a string holding a JSON object): every key, a dotted path into the event payload, must equal its value; an array value matches any of its elements, e.g. {"status":["done","error"]}. Default: every event on the topic.

command.description: Id of the agent-visible command to call, e.g. agents.prompt or agents.new.

args.description: Arguments of the command as JSON text, e.g. {"session":"<id>","text":"{{payload.session}} finished"}; default {}.

limit.description: Runs a minute (1–60) before the loop guard pauses the trigger; 0 or unset: 10.

parallel.description: true: a run starts while the previous one is still running instead of the event being dropped. Default false.

owner.description: self (default): the trigger belongs to your agent session, fires as you and is deleted when your session is closed. none: it outlives your session and fires with no caller. Triggers created by the user have no owner.

run.description: Id of the agent graph run (gr_…) the trigger is an edge of; only the Graphs plugin can set it; from any other caller it is ignored. The Triggers section groups the run's triggers under the run and offers Open graph instead of Delete.

runTitle.description: Title of that run, shown on the group row and as "created by graph <title>".

commands.title: List triggers
commands.description: List the workspace's triggers without their run history: {triggers: [{id, name, on, match?, command, args, enabled, limit?, parallel?, owner?, createdBy?, failures?, lastError?}]}. Non-destructive.

commands.title: Show trigger
commands.description: Show one trigger with its last 100 runs: history [{at, topic, seq, status, reason?, result?, chain?}] (chain: the session, cron job or trigger that led to the event) and paused [{from, to?, reason?}], status ok, error or skipped (busy, no app, previous run still running, owner gone, owner unknown, emitted by another agent session; skips are not failures). Non-destructive.

commands.title: Update trigger
commands.description: Change a trigger; only the given fields change; match "" or "{}" drops the filter. command and args are checked like in triggers.add. An agent may change only triggers owned or created by itself or its child sessions, or ones a plugin added (createdBy plugin:<id>). Returns the trigger. Non-destructive.

match.description: New payload filter as JSON text; "" drops it.

limit.description: Runs a minute (1–60) before the loop guard pauses the trigger; 0: back to 10.

parallel.description: true: a run starts while the previous one is still running instead of the event being dropped. Default false.

commands.title: Pause trigger
commands.description: Stop a trigger from firing until triggers.resume. An agent may pause only triggers owned or created by itself or its child sessions, or ones a plugin added (createdBy plugin:<id>). Returns the trigger. Non-destructive.

commands.title: Resume trigger
commands.description: Resume a paused trigger (also one paused by errors or the loop limit) and clear its failure count and last error. An agent may resume only triggers owned or created by itself or its child sessions, or ones a plugin added (createdBy plugin:<id>). Returns the trigger. Non-destructive.

commands.title: Delete trigger
commands.description: Delete a trigger. An agent may delete only triggers owned or created by itself or its child sessions, or ones a plugin added (createdBy plugin:<id>). Non-destructive.

commands.title: Emit event
commands.description: Publish the bus event event.<name> in this workspace, with payload plus workspace set to this workspace and by set to your agent session; an owned trigger whose args use placeholders ignores events emitted by sessions other than its owner and the owner's descendants; triggers listening on it fire. Schedule it with cron.add to run triggers on a timer. Returns {topic, seq}. Non-destructive.

name.description: Event name: lowercase dot-separated words, e.g. nightly or build.done; the topic is event.<name>.

payload.description: Event payload as JSON text (a string holding a JSON object); its workspace field is always this workspace.

cronJob.description: Id of the cron job (cj_…) that emits the event, put in the payload as cronJob; the cron plugin sets it and nobody else may.
